subject: Streaming concurrency playbook discussion — recap & immediate asks
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@nutra.ai>, Elena Park <ela@nutra.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming concurrency playbook discussion — recap & immediate asks

Tom / Elena,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to see the end-to-end flow and the areas causing production friction. Below is a short write-up so we have aligned expectations and concrete next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Top pain points you called out
- High tail latency on user-facing chat (spiky 500–900 ms for short prompts; worst-case >1s at peak).
- Streaming UX stalls: first-byte often delayed and then token delivery is bursty. Customers see janky typing effects.
- Concurrency limits force you to drop requests or degrade to a smaller model at peak.
- Cost overhead from CPU fallbacks and lack of effective token-level caching.

Current stack notes you shared
- Self-hosted Triton backends behind an nginx edge; autoscale via VM pool.
- Primary models are 13B variants—no quantized production builds yet.
- Simple request fan-out proxy, no prefix/KV cache in front of the model.

Success criteria (what would feel like a win)
- User-visible SLO: 200–300 ms p95 for conversational turns <512 tokens; 95th percentile steady stream first-byte <100 ms.
- Support 350–500 concurrent active user streams with graceful degradation policies.
- End-to-end cost reduction of ~30% by enabling batching/cache/quantized runtimes.

Short-term next steps (this week)
1) You: share a 30s sample trace and a short list of 10 representative prompts (you attached one trace; thanks).
2) Us (Redwood): spin up a quick proof harness on a dedicated trial pool to reproduce: a) streaming first-byte latency, b) token throughput over long turns, and c) max sustained concurrent streams.
3) Tech deep-dive: schedule a 60 min follow-up with your infra lead + our runtime engineer to review trace-level root causes and run a constrained load test (I proposed Tue/Wed morning PT).
4) Proposal: we will surface a concrete config: batching window, prefix cache rules, and a quantized model variant to hit the target SLOs.

Attachment: redwood-discovery-checklist.pdf (small checklist) and example-trace.txt

If that matches, I will book the deep-dive and loop in a runtime engineer.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Tom Nguyen <tom@nutra.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <ela@nutra.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 17:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming concurrency playbook discussion — recap & immediate asks

Rishi,

Thanks for the clear summary — that's exactly the set of issues. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Our observed steady-state tail is closer to 650–800 ms for short chat turns; spikes to ~1.2s under load.
- We do have a small cache at the proxy layer but it's cold most of the time since prompts are highly personalized.
- Security: we cannot push any customer data outside our VPC without an approved contract/controls; interested in your Private deployment option.

We've attached an extra trace and a short doc on our current autoscaling knobs. For the deep-dive, Tue 10am PT works for Elena and me. Please send a calendar invite.

Also curious: what minimal changes would you recommend to get streaming UX to feel smooth (without a full infra refactor)?

Cheers,
Tom
CTO, Nutra AI
tom@nutra.ai

---
Attached: extra-trace-1115.txt, autoscale-notes.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming concurrency playbook discussion — prep notes for Tue 10am PT deep-dive

Vivek / Marissa,

Looping you in with Tom's confirmation for Tuesday 10am PT. Quick internal prep notes so we show up with an execution plan:
- Primary ask: reproduce their steady-state scenario and show improvement vectors. We'll run two short experiments: 1) streaming-first-byte optimization (reduce initial scheduling + kernel warmup) and 2) concurrency stress to 500 active streams to validate queuing/backpressure.
- Targets to present: baseline metrics (their trace), expected delta with our default optimize profile, and one config example (prefix cache + 4ms batching window) that typically helps typing UX.
- Permissions: Nutra is sensitive about data leaving their VPC; prepare notes on Private deployment and our on-prem offering.
- Artifacts to bring: quick demo plan, cost delta estimate, and a short playbook PDF (use redwood-discovery-checklist.pdf as the base).

Action items
- Vivek: prototype the 4ms batching + prefix cache config on a small dedicated pool; capture sample traces. (Owner: Vivek)
- Marissa: draft a one-slide summary of cost vs latency tradeoffs for the meeting. (Owner: Marissa)
- Rishi: book the invite, produce the demo plan, and prepare a short script for the load tests. (Owner: Rishi)

I'll put the invite on their calendar and attach the demo plan to the meeting.

Thanks,
Rishi
